title: Evals: change-aware anomaly timeline and adaptive alert fan-out in Console
creator: Anika Rao
description:
Problem summary: Today our Evals system surfaces score regressions but lacks clear attribution and noisy alerting when multiple changes (model rollouts, config toggles, batching/quantization) occur concurrently. This leads to: repeated Slack/PagerDuty noise, engineering time spent chasing symptoms, and slow remediation.

Goal: Develop a change-aware Evals timeline and adaptive alert fan-out inside Console that ties regressions to recent deployments/config changes, reduces duplicate alerts, and routes high-confidence root-cause hints to the correct on-call or team. The feature should: generate a temporal view of eval score trends (per-test and per-promptset) with annotated change events (model version, quantization profile, runtime kernel change, autoscaling policy), compute regression fingerprints for deduplication, and implement configurable alert fan-out rules (Slack channels, PagerDuty escalation) with suppression/dedup windows and confidence thresholds.

Key user stories:
- As an SRE or ML engineer, I want a timeline that overlays eval score deltas with recent deployment metadata so I can quickly see which change likely triggered a drop.
- As a PM, I want alerts only when regressions exceed a configurable signal threshold after accounting for transient noise and rollout staging, and I want them routed to the responsible team instead of broadcasting to multiple channels.
- As an on-call, I want a single deduplicated incident per regression fingerprint with links to the failing prompt examples, PRs, and a quick-replay harness so I can triage faster.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Console timeline UI that shows per-eval metric trend with change annotations (model/config/deploy ID, author, link) for at least 90 days.
2) Backend correlation engine that ingests change events and computes candidate attributions with a confidence score (low|medium|high).
3) Alerting engine supports: grouping by regression fingerprint, suppression window (configurable per project), and fan-out rules to Slack and PagerDuty.
4) Alerts include: top failing prompt examples, before/after aggregate metric delta, likely attribution, and links to related PRs and promptset diffs.
5) Default routing maps: model/core infra regressions -> infra PagerDuty, promptset/quality regressions -> ML on-call Slack + PagerDuty if high confidence.
6) E2E test harness and runbook with rollback/canary guidance documented in Confluence.

Non-goals: building new eval metrics or replacing the eval scoring pipeline itself. This work focuses on attribution, UI, and alerting behavior.

Dependencies: change-event stream from deployment system (engineering work), Console UI annotation components, PagerDuty/Slack connector updates, replay sandbox for reproducing prompts.

Rollout plan: alpha for internal Redwood teams (infra + ML) for two weeks, followed by opt-in beta for select customers, then default-on with gradual aggressiveness tuning and per-tenant suppression presets.
comments: 2026-02-12 — Kickoff: cross-functional sync with Console, Runtime, and Alerts. Agreed to prototype timeline annotations using deployment webhook payloads and model-catalog metadata. Action: ENG to provide schema by 2026-02-19. — Anika Rao

2026-02-19 — Engineering provided change-event schema; includes deploy_id, actor, component_tags, kernel_profile, quantization_profile, batch_config, and commit link. Decided to store events in the evals-timeseries index with a change_event_id. Action: PM to draft attribution heuristics. — Luca Moreno

2026-02-25 — Design mockups reviewed: timeline with stacked annotations, hovercard with 'why likely cause' and link to PR + replay. Design requested a compact alert payload to avoid Slack flooding. Action: DES to add compact vs expanded alert templates. — Priya Singh (Design)

2026-03-03 — Decision: Use fingerprinting algorithm that combines metric signature (test id + metric delta pattern) and recent change_event_ids within a 48-hour window. Grouping window configurable per project. Trade-off: wider windows reduce duplicates but risk over-grouping unrelated regressions. Chosen default: 24-hour window. — Engineering

2026-03-08 — Compliance: security reviewed the payloads for Slack/PagerDuty. Redact prompt text in alerts by default, include 'top failures (redacted)' link to Console where access controls apply. Action: add KMS tagging to replay artifacts. — Security
notes: Consider later enhancements: automated rollback suggestions, A/B regret analysis for multi-variant rollouts, and per-customer suppression presets. Track metric-level baseline drift separately (future work).
